To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a new series of bis(9-amineacridine- 4-carboxamido) DNA-threading ligands with cytotoxicity towards HL-60 leukaemia cells and that we have shown that the presence of a charged side chain in a DNA- threading bis(9-acridinyl) ligand does not necessarily result in a decrease in cytotoxicity.
we have designed and synthesized a series of DNA-binding bis(9-amidoacridines) comprising ethyl-piperidino and methyl-piperidin-2-yl sidechains joined by neutral, charged or semi-rigid linkers.
the ethylp DNA threading bis(4-carboxamido-9-aminoacrydines): synthesis, cytotoxicity, and effects on the cell cycle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of DNA-threading molecules that are able to interact with DNA in a sequence-specific manner.
the synthesis and evaluation of novel DNA-threading bisacridines, which are potent inhibitors of cell proliferation, and their potential for the development of novel anticancer agents.
the development of DNA threading bis(9-acridinecarboxamide)s, which have potential as anti-cancer agents, as they are cytotoxic and cell cycle arrest inducing towards human leukaemia cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cytotoxicity is a complex function of the DNA binding, and the effects of the piperidine sidechain on the DNA binding and cytotoxicity are not straightforward.
the cytotoxicity of these compounds is not directly related to their binding to DNA.
the cytotoxicity of these compounds depends on a combination of factors, including DNA binding, cell uptake and cell cycle arrest.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DNA threading bis(9-acridinecarboxamides) are a promising new class of DNA binding drugs.

DNA threading is an important feature in the DNA binding of these compounds and that the cytotoxicity and DNA binding of these bisacridines is influenced by the nature of the linker between the two intercalating moieties.
the ethylpipedino series is generally more cytotoxic than its corresponding N-methylpipedino series, but that the latter series is more effective at inhibiting the G(2)-M phase of the cell cycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DNA threading bis(9-acridinyl) compounds are potent cytotoxic agents, with a range of sidechains giving IC(50) in the low micromolar range.
the ethylpieridino series has the best overall properties, with good DNA binding and cytotoxicity, and no significant cell cycle arrest.
the DNA threading bis(9-acridinecarboxamides) are cytotoxic towards human leukaemia cells, but the cytotoxicity does not correlate with DNA binding affinity.
